summary: Turns a live mono instrument into MIDI and lets the audio pass through (monitor blend 0 to 100 %). Melody mode (guitar, bass, keys, wind, synth lines): a note at each onset with its velocity from the attack, or at the first clean pitch; plucks, re-plucks, hammer-ons and slides handled; a minimum note length, legato, an optional key or scale lock, octave shift, and pitch bend (plus or minus 1 to 12 semitones) so slides and vibrato come through; Fast (the note plays as soon as its pitch is clear, and is corrected within 80 ms) or Stable (waits for a settled pitch). Drums mode (a drum kit, a pad, a percussive instrument): kick, snare and hat notes with no training, each with its own note, velocity, sensitivity and minimum interval, and an optional calibration of five hits each. The MIDI goes to a target machine, to an external MIDI device, and is a MIDI From source for armed tracks. Use it to play a synth from a guitar or bass, to turn a drum kit into a drum machine's triggers, or to record a performance as a clip.
use_for: Play a synth from a guitar, bass or keys and turn a drum kit into drum triggers: notes with velocity and pitch bend from a live mono instrument, and kick, snare and hat hits without training.

parameters.name: Monitor
parameters.description: Dry audio at the output: 0 is silent, 100 % is the input as it came
parameters.how: Sets how much of the dry instrument reaches the output, from 0% (silent) to 100% (as it came in).
parameters.sound: At 0% you hear only what the synth plays from the MIDI; a little dry signal gives the player a feel of the strings.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Melody: one note at a time, with its pitch. Drums: kick, snare and hat hits
parameters.how: Chooses what the input is turned into: a melody (notes with a pitch) or drum hits (kick, snare, hat).
parameters.sound: Melody follows the pitch of a guitar, bass or keys; Drums ignores pitch and names each hit by its sound.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: The lowest and highest note it listens for: Guitar (80 Hz to 1.2 kHz, about 16 ms), Bass (38 to 400 Hz, about 33 ms), Full (38 Hz to 2 kHz, about 33 ms)
parameters.how: Chooses the pitch range: Guitar (from 80 Hz, about 16 ms), Bass (from 38 Hz, about 33 ms) or Full (38 Hz to 2 kHz, about 33 ms).
parameters.sound: A narrower range answers sooner; Bass and Full see the lowest notes of a bass but each note starts a little later.

parameters.name: Level
parameters.description: The quietest signal that plays a note: under this level nothing starts
parameters.how: Sets the quietest level, from -70 to -20 dB, that starts a note or a hit.
parameters.sound: Raising it ignores amp hum, string noise and bleed; set too high it misses soft playing.

parameters.name: Sensitivity
parameters.description: How soft an attack may be and still start a note or a hit (the onset threshold)
parameters.how: Sets how soft an attack may be and still count, from 0 to 100%.
parameters.sound: Higher values catch soft plucks and ghost notes and risk noise, fret buzz and bleed.

parameters.name: Response
parameters.description: Fast plays a note as soon as its pitch is clear and corrects it within 80 ms; Stable waits Settle ms first
parameters.how: Chooses when a new note starts: Fast plays it at the first clean pitch and corrects it within 80 ms if it was another note (or by pitch bend when that is on); Stable waits Settle ms of the same note before playing it.
parameters.sound: Fast feels immediate for live playing and may retrigger once on a muddy attack; Stable never plays a wrong first note but answers later.

parameters.name: Retrigger
parameters.description: A new attack of the note already sounding plays it again (a re-pluck); off ignores attacks while a note sounds
parameters.how: Switches playing a note again on each new attack, even of the same pitch, on or off.
parameters.sound: On, every pluck of the same string plays a new note; off suits sustained instruments whose attack is not a new note.

parameters.name: Lock
parameters.description: Off: every semitone. Set key: the Root and Scale. Song key: the key of the song (the song's Key entry), else Root and Scale. Suggest: the key found from the notes played so far
parameters.how: Chooses how notes are kept to a key: Off, the Root and Scale, the song's key or a key found from what you played.
parameters.sound: Locked notes land on the key whatever the instrument does; Off follows every semitone, which is what most instruments want.

parameters.name: Root
parameters.description: The key's root note
parameters.how: Sets the key's root note from C to B.
parameters.sound: It moves every in-key note with it; the scale keyboard shows the result.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: The scale the notes are locked to
parameters.how: Chooses the scale of the key from 14 choices, including a Custom set of notes.
parameters.sound: Major sounds bright, minor darker, pentatonic and blues leave out the notes that clash.

parameters.name: Custom notes
parameters.description: The notes of the Custom scale, one bit per note from C (bit 0) to B
parameters.how: Holds the Custom scale's twelve notes, one bit each from C to B.
parameters.sound: Only the notes you switch on in the keyboard can play when Scale is Custom.

parameters.name: Octave
parameters.description: Octave shift of the notes
parameters.how: Shifts the notes by whole octaves, from -3 to +3.
parameters.sound: A bass can play a synth bass an octave higher, or a guitar a synth lead two octaves up.

parameters.name: Stickiness
parameters.description: How far past the middle between two notes the pitch must go before the note changes (a hysteresis)
parameters.how: Sets how far past the middle between two notes the pitch must go before the note changes, from 0 to 100 cents.
parameters.sound: More stickiness holds a bent or wobbly note steady; none follows every small move.

parameters.name: Settle
parameters.description: How long a new pitch must be held before it replaces the note sounding (and, in Stable response, before a note first plays)
parameters.how: Sets how long a new pitch must be held before it replaces the note sounding, from 0 to 200 ms; in Stable response it also delays the first note.
parameters.sound: Longer settling removes grace notes and brief slides at the cost of a later note start.

parameters.name: Min note length
parameters.description: A note lasts at least this long, however short the sound was
parameters.how: Sets the shortest a note lasts, from 0 to 100 mapped to 0 to 500 ms.
parameters.sound: Short plucked notes still last long enough for the synth to sound.

parameters.name: Release
parameters.description: The note ends when the level falls this far under its peak (or the pitch is lost)
parameters.how: Sets how far the level must fall under the note's peak, from 6 to 40 dB, before the note ends.
parameters.sound: A small drop ends notes with the pluck; a large one lets them ring out with the string's decay.

parameters.name: Legato
parameters.description: A new note starts before the old one stops (for mono synths with legato), instead of after
parameters.how: Starts a new note before the old one stops when switched on.
parameters.sound: Mono synths then glide between notes instead of retriggering.

parameters.name: Pitch bend
parameters.description: Pitch bend range: the pitch's distance from the note is sent as bend, so slides and vibrato come through. Set the same range on the synth
parameters.how: Sets the pitch bend range from off to plus or minus 12 semitones.
parameters.sound: Slides, bends and vibrato of the instrument move the synth's pitch by the same amount; set the synth to the same range.

parameters.name: Bend mode
parameters.description: Free: bend follows every wobble. Anchored: the note stays put until the pitch moves farther than the Anchor from its middle, then it bends
parameters.how: Chooses Free bend or Anchored bend.
parameters.sound: Free follows every wobble; Anchored keeps the note still until the pitch leaves it, then bends.

parameters.name: Anchor
parameters.description: Anchored bend: how far from the note's middle the pitch must move before the bend starts
parameters.how: Sets how far from the note's middle the pitch must move, from 5 to 100 cents, before the bend starts.
parameters.sound: A larger anchor keeps vibrato from bending the note; a small one bends at once.

parameters.name: Velocity
parameters.description: Dynamic: from how hard the note was attacked. Fixed: always the Fixed velocity
parameters.how: Chooses note velocity from the attack (Dynamic) or always the Fixed velocity.
parameters.sound: Dynamic plays soft picking softly; Fixed gives every note the same strength.

parameters.name: Fixed velocity
parameters.description: The velocity of every note in Fixed mode, and the loudest in Dynamic
parameters.how: Sets the fixed velocity, and the loudest in Dynamic, from 1 to 127.
parameters.sound: Higher values play louder or brighter on most synths.

parameters.name: Softest velocity
parameters.description: Dynamic: the velocity of the softest note
parameters.how: Sets the velocity of the softest note in Dynamic mode, from 1 to 127.
parameters.sound: A higher minimum keeps soft notes audible.

parameters.name: Soft level
parameters.description: Dynamic: the attack level that gives the softest velocity
parameters.how: Sets the attack level, from -70 to -20 dB, that gives the softest velocity.
parameters.sound: Raise it if soft playing sounds too loud on the synth.

parameters.name: Loud level
parameters.description: Dynamic: the attack level that gives the loudest velocity
parameters.how: Sets the attack level, from -40 to 0 dB, that gives the loudest velocity.
parameters.sound: Lower it so ordinary playing reaches full velocity.

parameters.name: Note channel
parameters.description: MIDI channel of the notes
parameters.how: Sets the MIDI channel of the notes, from 1 to 16.
parameters.sound: It selects which synth or part plays the line.

parameters.name: Hit length
parameters.description: How long each drum note is held before its note off
parameters.how: Sets how long each drum note is held, from 10 to 500 ms.
parameters.sound: Short notes suit drums that ring by themselves; long ones suit sustained sounds.

parameters.name: Drum channel
parameters.description: MIDI channel of the drum notes (10 is the drum channel)
parameters.how: Sets the MIDI channel of the drum notes, from 1 to 16.
parameters.sound: Channel 10 is the drum channel of most drum machines.

parameters.name: Kick note
parameters.description: MIDI note of the kick
parameters.how: Sets the MIDI note the kick plays, from 0 to 127.
parameters.sound: Choose the drum you want the kick to play; the default follows the usual drum map.

parameters.name: Kick velocity
parameters.description: 0: from how hard the hit was. 1 to 127: always this velocity
parameters.how: Sets the kick's velocity from 1 to 127, or 0 to take it from how hard the hit was.
parameters.sound: Zero makes harder hits play louder; a number makes every hit the same.

parameters.name: Kick sensitivity
parameters.description: How readily a hit counts as a kick: higher plays more of the doubtful hits
parameters.how: Sets how readily a hit counts as a kick, from 0 to 100%.
parameters.sound: Higher values play more kicks but let other drums through as one; lower ones play only clear kicks.

parameters.name: Kick interval
parameters.description: The shortest time between two kicks
parameters.how: Sets the shortest time between two kicks, from 10 to 300 ms.
parameters.sound: A kick's tail can look like a second hit; a longer interval ignores it, a short one lets double kicks through.

parameters.name: Snare note
parameters.description: MIDI note of the snare
parameters.how: Sets the MIDI note the snare plays, from 0 to 127.
parameters.sound: Choose the drum you want the snare to play; the default follows the usual drum map.

parameters.name: Snare velocity
parameters.description: 0: from how hard the hit was. 1 to 127: always this velocity
parameters.how: Sets the snare's velocity from 1 to 127, or 0 to take it from how hard the hit was.
parameters.sound: Zero makes harder hits play louder, ghost notes included; a number makes every hit the same.

parameters.name: Snare sensitivity
parameters.description: How readily a hit counts as a snare: higher plays more of the doubtful hits
parameters.how: Sets how readily a hit counts as a snare, from 0 to 100%.
parameters.sound: Higher values play more snares and ghost notes but let other drums through as one.

parameters.name: Snare interval
parameters.description: The shortest time between two snare hits
parameters.how: Sets the shortest time between two snare hits, from 10 to 300 ms.
parameters.sound: Long enough to ignore a rim's ring, short enough for rolls and ghost notes.

parameters.name: Hat note
parameters.description: MIDI note of the hat
parameters.how: Sets the MIDI note the hat plays, from 0 to 127.
parameters.sound: Choose the drum you want the hat to play; the default is the closed hat.

parameters.name: Hat velocity
parameters.description: 0: from how hard the hit was. 1 to 127: always this velocity
parameters.how: Sets the hat's velocity from 1 to 127, or 0 to take it from how hard the hit was.
parameters.sound: Zero makes harder hits play louder; a number makes every hit the same.

parameters.name: Hat sensitivity
parameters.description: How readily a hit counts as a hat: higher plays more of the doubtful hits
parameters.how: Sets how readily a hit counts as a hat, from 0 to 100%.
parameters.sound: Higher values play more hat hits but let the snare's wires and cymbals through as one.

parameters.name: Hat interval
parameters.description: The shortest time between two hat hits
parameters.how: Sets the shortest time between two hat hits, from 10 to 300 ms.
parameters.sound: Hats run fast: a short interval lets sixteenths and thirty-seconds through.

parameters.name: Record at attack
parameters.description: An armed track that records from this machine places each note at its attack, not at the moment it was sent; the sound you hear and what the target plays are unchanged
parameters.how: Switches recording at the attack on or off.
parameters.sound: On, a recorded take lines up with the playing even when the note was sent a few tens of milliseconds after the attack; off records each note when it was sent.
